analysis.title: When a Credit Default Swap Isn't about Credit
key_insights: Corporate CDS protection volume on AI-linked names rose 5x in three months per David Bahnsen's Dividend Cafe, and total corporate CDS volume in nine months of 2026 exceeds all of 2025. Names cited include Oracle, SpaceX, Google, Amazon, Meta, Broadcom and Nvidia.

Bahnsen argues the CDS surge is largely a by-product of volume and hedging, not default fear. AI-affiliated debt issuance was about $100B last year and has passed $466B so far in 2026, so more insurance follows more debt. Buyers hedge existing exposure to free up room to buy more of the debt.

Meta and Nvidia CDS spreads each widened more than 100 basis points. Bahnsen does not expect senior debt defaults at these issuers, and distinguishes that from risk to their equity. Mauldin says credit problems in AI will not stay contained to AI and will affect the wider economy, global markets and sovereign borrowing costs.

Deals cited for the week: Broadcom's $63B Anthropic financing vehicle, Meta's $95B stock sale, neoclouds still shut out of credit, SK Hynix memory sold out through 2029, rising GPU rental prices, Google selling TPUs to OpenAI and Oracle, and a relief rally led by optics stocks. Potential trillion-dollar IPOs are also mentioned.

Anthropic's IPO disclosures show an $80.7B net loss in the first half of 2026. Per Yahoo, $72.4B is a non-cash accounting charge from the rising value of convertible notes, and similar paper charges make up the rest. Operating loss for the six months was $693M, with a Q1 loss offset by a Q2 profit of $974M.

AI tools are finding existing software exploits faster than manual hackers. A PHP vulnerability became public last week. PHP runs on about 70% of systems worldwide per the letter. Microsoft had already fixed it, so the impact was minimal. Mauldin warns the next one may not go as well.

Cloudflare's CEO said the next two years will be 'incredibly fraught' with tools that search the internet for vulnerabilities. Cognition CISO Alex Stamos said security firms are backlogged with urgent patches and have no spare capacity.

Jacob Shapiro frames AI-driven cyber risk as a sovereignty issue, with governments needing to control data and move critical systems into protected environments. Mauldin raises the unresolved question of who regulates AI and notes the risk of constraining US development while racing China.

BCA Research's AI update shows AI compute rising faster, each lead lasting a shorter time, and no company holding a comfortable lead. China's competitive models have closed the roughly six-month gap to US models seen a few years ago. Mauldin asks whether the US can afford the capital cost of winning the race.

BCA's Matt Dyson notes AMD is beginning to catch up with Nvidia. Mauldin concludes Nvidia cannot maintain 70% margins. The three main memory chip makers face little competition, and DRAM prices are up 400-500% in the last year.

market_movers.rationale: Mauldin says AMD is catching up and Nvidia cannot maintain 70% margins. Nvidia's CDS spread widened over 100 basis points, which Bahnsen attributes to hedging and liquidity rather than default fear.
The cost of insuring Oracle's debt has risen sharply in recent months. Bahnsen attributes the move mostly to hedging demand and market technicals.
Meta's CDS spread widened over 100 basis points. The letter also cites a $95B Meta stock sale in the past week.
BCA's Matt Dyson observes AMD is beginning to catch up with Nvidia on chip performance.

sector_views.rationale: Memory makers have little competition and DRAM prices rose 400-500% in a year, while Nvidia's margin lead is eroding as AMD and others close the gap.
AI capex is large enough to affect GDP and credit markets. The letter flags financing strain and a cybersecurity vulnerability backlog as risks.

earnings_insights: Anthropic reported an $80.7B net loss for H1 2026, of which $72.4B is a non-cash charge from revaluing convertible notes. Operating loss was $693M for the half, with a Q2 operating profit of $974M against a Q1 loss (figures from Anthropic's IPO disclosures as cited from Yahoo, reported).

Neoclouds remain shut out of credit markets.
AI-found software vulnerabilities could hit critical infrastructure, with security firms backlogged on patches.
Regulation of AI may be poorly designed or may slow US development relative to China.
Nvidia margin compression as AMD and others catch up.

vol_and_positioning: CDS protection volume on AI-linked issuers is up 5x in three months. Meta and Nvidia CDS spreads widened over 100 basis points. Bahnsen attributes this to hedging needs and liquidity rather than default expectations.
geopolitical: US-China AI race: China's models have closed the gap with US models, and Mauldin says the West must not be subject to blackmail.
Cyber sovereignty: AI-found exploits pose risks to state critical infrastructure, per Jacob Shapiro, including from state-backed hacking groups.
Possible US AI regulation weighed against competition with China.

tension_points.bull_case: Bahnsen says the 5x rise in CDS volume reflects more AI debt issuance ($466B+ in 2026 vs about $100B in 2025) and hedging needed to take on more exposure, not default fear. He does not expect senior debt defaults at the issuers.
tension_points.bear_case: Mauldin says credit problems in AI will not stay contained and will affect the broader economy and sovereign borrowing costs. Neoclouds remain shut out of credit, and Bahnsen separates equity risk from senior debt risk.
